transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I just can’t make myself do anything anymore. I mostly sit in my room, and I’ll realize I’m still wearing the same clothes and I didn’t even think to change. I used to knit sometimes, and journal, and I’d go walking—there’s this one street near my house with really uneven sidewalks, I always noticed that—but now I just don’t do any of it.

My mom keeps asking me what’s wrong, and I don’t even know how to answer her. It feels like it takes too much energy just to say anything.
How long have you been feeling this way, with not wanting to do anything and having low energy?

Um… I think it’s been since I started that community-college program. So… like two years ago? Actually a little more—two years and maybe two months. It kind of all started slipping around then, though I didn’t notice it right away because I was trying to keep track of classes and the bus schedule, and there was this vending machine near the hallway that always took my coins but… yeah. Since then, really.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, like activities you did before such as knitting, journaling, or walking?

Yeah… I don’t really enjoy them now. I mean, knitting used to feel… kind of calming, like counting the stitches, and I had this blue yarn that got all tangled in a drawer, but now I just look at it and don’t do anything. Same with journaling. I’ll think maybe I should write something, and then I just sit there.

Walking too—I used to go out more, even just around the block, but now it’s like I can’t make myself leave my room. I’ll be in the same clothes and not even really notice. When my mom asks what’s wrong, I barely have the energy to answer her.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not worth much lately?

I don’t… I don’t know. Not really like guilt, I guess? I mean, sometimes my mom says things and I can tell she’s tired, and then I start thinking about the dishes in the sink or how the light in the hallway flickers and nobody fixes it, but… I don’t know if that’s the same thing.

Worth much… I’m not sure how to answer that. I mostly just feel kind of blank. Like I’m there, but not doing anything.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately, like not being able to fall asleep or waking up too early, or on the flip side, do you find yourself sleeping much more than usual?

I’m… not really sure. I don’t keep track of it very well. Sometimes I’m in bed for a long time, but I don’t know if I’m sleeping or just lying there, you know? The clock has those red numbers and they kind of make the room look strange at night, and then I start thinking about whether I left a cup on the floor.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern, I guess.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed. Like… I’m not crying all day or anything. It’s more like everything is kind of far away, or quiet, even when the TV is on.

Some days I look out the window and the same car is parked there, the red one with the dent, and I’ll just keep staring at it and then it’s like an hour passed. But I don’t know if that means I’m down. I just feel… not much, I guess.
Have you ever felt like life isn’t worth living or had thoughts about harming yourself?

I don’t… I don’t really know how to answer that. Life being worth living sounds like one of those things people say on posters at school, like in the counselor’s office, with the ocean picture behind it.

I haven’t really… I mean, I don’t sit there planning anything, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes I just kind of don’t think about it at all. Like I’ll be holding a spoon and then notice the pattern on it, and it’s like everything goes quiet for a while.

So… I’m not sure. I don’t think I have a clear answer.
Have you noticed that you move or speak more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, that you’re more restless or fidgety than before?

I guess… slower, maybe. Not like I’m trying to be. I just sit in my room and it’s like I can’t get started on anything. I’ll still be wearing the same clothes, and my mom comes in and asks what’s wrong, but answering feels like… too much work.

I used to knit sometimes, and write in my journal, and I’d go walk around the block, especially when the sky looked kind of orange in the evening. There was this one house with little ceramic ducks by the steps, and I always wondered why they faced the street instead of the door… but I don’t really do that now. Mostly I just sit there. I don’t feel fidgety. It’s more like everything takes too much effort, even talking.
Have you noticed that your movements, like walking or doing simple tasks, have become slower than usual?

Yeah… I think so. Like, walking, I don’t know, but doing things feels slow because I just can’t make myself start. I’ll sit in my room in the same clothes and it’s like the whole day gets thick or something.

I used to knit, and I had this journal with a blue cover—there was a little rip near the corner because I kept it in my backpack with pens loose in there—but I don’t really pick it up now. And walking too, I used to go out sometimes, just around the block, but now I just… don’t.

When my mom asks me what’s wrong, I barely answer. Not because I’m mad at her. It just takes too much energy to make the words come out.
Can you tell me more about how you feel when you try to do things you used to enjoy, like knitting or walking—do you feel any interest or pleasure in them at all now?

I don’t really feel… much interest, no. Like I look at the knitting bag and it’s just there. The yarn kind of spills out of it sometimes because the zipper catches, and I used to like choosing colors, but now it feels like something across the room that belongs to someone else.

Walking is the same. I used to go around the block, and there’s that house with the ducks by the steps—I think I told you that already—but I don’t go see them now. I mostly just sit in my room with the same clothes on, and then hours pass. My journal’s there too, but I don’t write.

It’s not exactly that I hate those things. I just can’t make myself do them, and if my mom asks what’s wrong, even answering her feels like too much energy.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating much less than before or losing weight without trying?

I don’t know… I haven’t really kept track. My mom cooks sometimes and there’ll be plates in the sink, and I’ll think about how the spoon always gets left in the bowl and then it dries like that, and it’s hard to wash after.

But appetite… I mean, I don’t think I noticed losing weight or anything. My clothes feel the same, I guess. I eat when food is there sometimes. I’m not sure if it’s less than before. I don’t really pay attention to it.
Would you say that you have been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t know if “depressed” is the right word. Like… I don’t wake up and think that word exactly. It’s more like the day is just sitting there, if that makes sense.

Sometimes the light comes through the blinds in stripes, and I’ll stare at that for a long time, and then I realize I was supposed to get up or do something. My mom says the house gets quiet when I’m like this, but houses make sounds anyway—like the fridge clicks and the pipes do that tapping thing.

So… most of the day? I’m not sure. I guess I don’t feel good, but I don’t know if it’s sad or down exactly. It’s more blank.
Would you say that you have completely lost interest in everything, to the point where nothing really holds your attention or feels meaningful anymore?

I mean… completely, I don’t know. That sounds like a big word. But mostly, yeah, nothing really pulls me toward it anymore.

I just sit in my room a lot, in the same clothes, and the knitting bag is there and my journal is there, but I don’t pick them up. I used to walk too, like around the block, but now even thinking about shoes and the door and all that feels like too much.

And when my mom asks what’s wrong, I can hear her, but answering feels… heavy. Like I don’t have enough in me to even explain it.
Would you say that you’ve felt a loss of energy or unexplained fatigue nearly every day, even when you haven’t done anything physically taxing?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not like I ran or did anything, I’m just… there.

Mostly I sit in my room, and I’ll still be in the same clothes, and the stuff is right there—my knitting bag, my journal—and I look at it but I don’t do it. I used to go walking, but now even that feels like there are too many steps before the actual walking, like finding socks and shoes and opening the door.

And my mom will ask what’s wrong, and I hear her, I do, but answering feels like trying to lift something heavy. Like I don’t even have enough energy to explain.
Would you say that you have felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for most of the past two years?

Two years… I don’t know. That’s hard to measure. I don’t really keep it in like… blocks like that.

I know there have been long stretches where things felt kind of gray, like the same day repeating, but then I start thinking about school being over and how the calendar in the kitchen still has an old month on it, and my mom keeps saying she’ll change it but she doesn’t. So time gets weird.

Most of the day, nearly every day… I can’t say that exactly. I’m not sure. It’s been a while, but I don’t know if I can put two years on it.
Would you say that you have felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two years?

I still don’t know how to answer that exactly. Two years sounds so… measured, like I should have been marking it on a calendar or something.

I know there’s been a lot of time where I feel low, or like everything is kind of muted, but then some days I can’t tell if it’s depressed or just tired or just the day being weird. And the past two years had so many little pieces in it—school ending, being home more, my mom asking things, the same room—so it all kind of blends together.

So… I can’t really say “yes, most of the day, nearly every day, for two years.” I’m not sure.
Would you say that for the past two years, most days you felt down or depressed for most of the day?

I’m still not sure. Like… “most days” maybe sounds closer than saying exactly every day, but “for most of the day” is the part where I get stuck.

Some days I wake up and it’s already heavy, and then I’ll look at the window and the light is different by the time I notice I haven’t really done anything. But then I think maybe that’s just because the blinds are bent on one side and the sun comes in weird, and I end up staring at that instead of knowing what I feel.

So… I don’t know if I can say it that clearly. It’s been a lot of low days, I think, but I can’t measure it right.
Would you say that on most days over the past two years, you felt down or depressed, even if just for part of the day?

I mean… part of the day is maybe easier, but I still don’t know if I can put it on “most days” for two whole years.

There were a lot of days where I felt low for a while, yeah, but then I get mixed up because sometimes it’s just like I’m sitting there and the day sort of goes by, and I can’t tell if that counts as depressed or just… nothing. Like when you leave a cup in your room and keep seeing it but don’t move it, and then after a while it feels like it’s always been there.

So I don’t know. I can say it’s happened a lot, but I’m not sure about most days over two years.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about persistent depressed mood most of the day nearly every day over two years, but the provided symptom profile does not include a depressive mood symptom; the duration item only describes the overall decline, not depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Two years… I don’t know. That’s hard to measure. I don’t really keep it in like… blocks like that.

I know there have been long stretches where things felt kind of gray, like the same day repeating, but then I start thinking about school being over and how the calendar in the kitchen still has an old month on it, and my mom keeps saying she’ll change it but she doesn’t. So time gets weird.

Most of the day, nearly every day… I can’t say that exactly. I’m not sure. It’s been a while, but I don’t know if I can put two years on it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a persistent depressed mood for most of the day, on most days, for at least the past 2 years.
doctor.question: Would you say that you have felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two years?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about depressed mood most of the day nearly every day for two years, but the provided symptom profile does not include a depressive mood symptom; the duration item refers to the overall decline, not persistent depressed mood.

patient.answer:
I still don’t know how to answer that exactly. Two years sounds so… measured, like I should have been marking it on a calendar or something.

I know there’s been a lot of time where I feel low, or like everything is kind of muted, but then some days I can’t tell if it’s depressed or just tired or just the day being weird. And the past two years had so many little pieces in it—school ending, being home more, my mom asking things, the same room—so it all kind of blends together.

So… I can’t really say “yes, most of the day, nearly every day, for two years.” I’m not sure.

This uncertainty prevents definitive subcategorization into F33.2 (recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe), F33.1 (recurrent depressive disorder, current episode moderate), or F33.0 (recurrent depressive disorder, current episode mild) at this time.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood for the majority of the day, nearly every day, for at least two years, which is a key criterion for persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).
doctor.question: Would you say that for the past two years, most days you felt down or depressed for most of the day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about persistent depressed mood over the past two years, which is not one of the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m still not sure. Like… “most days” maybe sounds closer than saying exactly every day, but “for most of the day” is the part where I get stuck.

Some days I wake up and it’s already heavy, and then I’ll look at the window and the light is different by the time I notice I haven’t really done anything. But then I think maybe that’s just because the blinds are bent on one side and the sun comes in weird, and I end up staring at that instead of knowing what I feel.

So… I don’t know if I can say it that clearly. It’s been a lot of low days, I think, but I can’t measure it right.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood for at least 2 years, with some days being relatively free of symptoms, which would support a diagnosis of Persistent Depressive Disorder (F34.1) rather than Major Depressive Disorder (F32.x) or Recurrent Depressive Disorder (F33.x).
doctor.question: Would you say that on most days over the past two years, you felt down or depressed, even if just for part of the day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about persistent depressed mood over the past two years, but the provided symptom profile does not include a depressive mood symptom item.

patient.answer:
I mean… part of the day is maybe easier, but I still don’t know if I can put it on “most days” for two whole years.

There were a lot of days where I felt low for a while, yeah, but then I get mixed up because sometimes it’s just like I’m sitting there and the day sort of goes by, and I can’t tell if that counts as depressed or just… nothing. Like when you leave a cup in your room and keep seeing it but don’t move it, and then after a while it feels like it’s always been there.

So I don’t know. I can say it’s happened a lot, but I’m not sure about most days over two years.
